evidence: Cic. ND 2.151: nōs onera quibusdam bēstiīs, nōs juga impōnimus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The same word is a pair of animals, a cross-bar, and the ridge of a hill.

phrases.latin: aspice, arātra jugō referunt suspēnsa juvencī
phrases.english: look, the bullocks are bringing home the ploughs hung from the yoke

phrases.latin: rōbustus quoque jam taurīs juga solvet arātor
phrases.english: the sturdy ploughman too will now take the yoke off his bulls

sources: Lewis & Short: jugum
